Full release notes: **https://danbyte.net/news/v0-16-0**

### New in 0.16.6

#### Security

- **Export templates render only what the caller may view, and never a credential.** The render path scoped rows by tenant alone, so a site-scoped user got the whole tenant, and a template could name a webhook or automation target as its subject and print its decrypted secret and Authorization header. Rows now pass the same row/site restriction as the lists, types that carry credentials cannot be a template's subject, and a secret field or PSK accessor is unreadable from any row a template reaches. (#193)
- **Rendered output is always an inert download.** A template declaring `text/html` was served inline on the app's origin, which let a template author run script for whoever opened it. Renders now download as plain text unless the declared type is CSV, JSON, XML, YAML or plain text, with `nosniff` set. (#195)
- **Webhook header names no longer echo a folded value.** A header line without a colon was returned whole as a "name". Only well-formed `Name: value` lines contribute a name. (#194)
- **A bulk-rename pattern cannot hold a worker.** A user regex runs under a match deadline and a length cap, and a compliance rule's pattern the same. A pattern that takes too long is refused with a field error. (#202)

#### Fixed

- **Change log labels survive a malformed stored id.** One bad primary key in a page's diffs blanked every label of that model on the page; it now costs only its own label. (#199)
- **VRF list costs the same at any size.** Prefix, VLAN and address counts per VRF come with the page instead of three queries per row. (#196)
- **Check materialisation no longer loads every prefix per address.** A pass builds one prefix index per tenant and resolves each address against it, and the candidate scan reads the tenant's addresses once instead of once per prefix assignment. (#198)
- **Compliance evaluates each object type in one scan** whatever the number of rules on it. (#200)
- **The dashboard's scope and family distributions are grouped counts in the database**, not every address parsed in Python. (#201)
- **A save indexes its tags once, and an import indexes each row once at the end** rather than inline per save; a dry run indexes nothing. (#197)

#### Upgrading

- New Python dependency `regex`. A git install picks it up with the upgrade's dependency step; the bundle ships the wheel.

#### Added

- **The id on a label finds its object.** Typing the number a flag shows (`206`) or the first characters of the object's UUID (`d4d9c41c`) into any list's search box matches it; a number matches `numid` exactly, six or more hex characters match the start of the UUID. Every list endpoint of a numbered type takes `?numid=<n>` instead of ignoring it. Labels gain `{{ short_hex }}`, the first eight characters of the UUID, and `{{ short_id }}` falls back to it on an object with no number yet.
